newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-GREENE ENDS LONG U.S. WAIT FOR 100 GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GREENE ENDS LONG U.S. WAIT FOR 100 GOLD.

text.p: Maurice Greene became the first American man for six years to win a major 100 metres title when he equalled the third fastest time ever in the world championships final on Sunday.

Greene, 23, lived up to his nickname of the "Kansas Cannonball" by blasting away the opposition at the Athens Olympic stadium in 9.86 seconds, just two hundredths of a second outside the world record.
Canadian Donovan Bailey, who set the mark in last year's Atlanta Olympic final, relinquished his world title to Greene whose consistency before the final provided the foundation of his victory.

The American world champion had run four successive times of 9.90 seconds and, despite cramps before the final, was able to move up a gear, clock a lifetime best and bring the United States its first global 100 title since Carl Lewis won in Tokyo in 1991.

"I am an American and that's what I came here for, to get the gold medal for the United States. I just feel very excited and I thank the Lord for giving me the energy and strength to do it," Greene said.

"Ever since I started training for the world championships last September I believed I could be the fastest man in the world. I thought the world record would fall today but it didn't and that's my next goal, to break the world record."

Bailey, who never looked at his best after struggling with cramp in the opening two rounds on Saturday, still took the silver in 9.91 seconds, ahead of American Tim Montgomery who won the bronze in 9.94 seconds.

Bailey said: "I'm not really disappointed. I have lost 12 pounds (five kg) since I last competed in Europe, but I am not going to sit here and make excuses. I'm second. When I looked at him as we crossed the line in the semifinal I wanted to look into his eye and tell him I am still the man."
The surprise of the race was the disappointing performance of Trinidadian Ato Boldon, who looked in outstanding form in the second round on Saturday when he clocked 9.87 seconds.

Boldon, who like Greene is coached by John Smith, the 440 yards world record holder, looked even more at ease in the semifinals earlier on Sunday when he clocked 10.00 seconds easing up over the last 25 metres.
But he said he was suffering from cramp as soon as he got out of the starting blocks.
"I knew I had problems immediatly," he said. "But I will have another chance in the 200 and I am keeping my head for that. I am truly delighted for Maurice. He deserves it."

Greene's victory, coupled with Marion Jones's win in the women's 100 final a few minutes earlier, completed an American sprint double in the event at a global championships for the first time since Lewis and Florence Griffith Joyner won golds in Seoul at the 1988 Olympics.

Lewis's victory came after Ben Johnson was disqualified for doping and Sunday night was the first time two Americans have crossed the finish line first in the 100 since Lewis and Evelyn Ashford won their respective titles at the Los Angeles Olympics 13 years ago.
